candidates.title: Proton-Boron (p11B) Fuel Arrives — LPP Fusion
candidates.notes: Accessible. Contains LPPFusion's actual procurement data: $56,000 for 93g of 99.9% B-11 enriched decaborane ($600/g = $600,000/kg at lab scale). Two-country production: isotopic boron from Russia, decaborane compound from Czech Republic. Notes mass production could reduce cost 'many hundred-fold'. Company blog post but the only source with a concrete transaction price.

entries.notes: Lab-scale cost confirmed ($600/g custom production). Commercial-scale cost not quantified — LPPFusion states 'many hundred-fold' reduction from mass production but gives no engineering basis. No peer-reviewed or government source found with enriched decaborane commercial pricing. The semiconductor 11BF3 pricing (~$9,500/kg peak) is for a different compound and different enrichment levels (99.8% for semiconductors vs 99.9% B-11 for fusion).

candidates.title: Diamond Photoconductive Semiconductor Switch (PCSS) — LLNL Innovation and Partnerships Office
candidates.notes: Accessible. LLNL government laboratory technology licensing page. Confirms diamond PCSS at TRL 3 (early research). Applications include pulsed power and high-frequency switching. Efficiency ~20%, output power ~50 kW. No commercial availability; technology available for licensing. Establishes that the technology LPPFusion proposes for its ion beam decelerator is at an early research stage.

entries.notes: Search revealed useful market context: 11BF3 (boron-11 trifluoride) is commercially produced at semiconductor scale by 3M, URENCO (15 MT/year of 99.99% enrichment from Dutch facility), and Chinese producers. The semiconductor industry is the primary commercial driver for enriched B-11. Pricing of ~$15,000/kg for 11BF3 appeared in one search summary but could not be traced to an accessible credible primary source. Note: LPPFusion uses decaborane (B10H14), not BF3 — the compound synthesis step adds additional cost beyond isotopic enrichment. No accessible source with quantitative commercial pricing for enriched decaborane specifically was found.

candidates.title: US team reinvents the photoconductive switch — Compound Semiconductor
candidates.notes: Accessible, original reporting on LLNL diamond PCSS breakthrough. Key parameters: on/off ratio >10^11, 2 ns rise/fall times, 44 A/cm2 current density at 60V DC bias, critical field 10 MV/cm. Mentions Opcondys Inc. as LLNL licensee and DOE ULTRAFAST program. Does NOT contain lifetime data (shots or hours) or commercial pricing — but documents current commercialization status.

candidates.title: Photoconductive Switch Enhancements and Lifetime Studies (DTIC)
candidates.notes: DTIC PDF report on PCSS lifetime studies — not fetched due to triage budget. Would likely be binary PDF with same access issues as OSTI PDF.

entries.notes: Search context from summaries (not primary sources): GaAs PCSS lifetimes range from ~10^4 shots (UWB-HPM applications at higher current) to ~10^8 shots (electro-optic drivers at 20A/5ns pulses). Diamond is expected to substantially exceed GaAs lifetime due to superior thermal conductivity (2100 W/m·K) and critical field (10 MV/cm). Commercial readiness: Opcondys Inc. (LLNL licensee) is developing commercial diamond PCSS under DOE ULTRAFAST funding — pre-commercial as of available information. The OSTI PCSS lifetime testing paper (biblio/1147822) is the most directly relevant source but was inaccessible as a binary PDF. Gap remains partially addressed — no direct diamond PCSS lifetime data found.
